newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai '96 retail sales hit record $14 billion.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai '96 retail sales hit record $14 billion.

text.p: Retail sales in Shanghai, China's biggest city and its economic hub, hit a record $14 billion in 1996, up almost 20 percent on the previous year, the China Daily Business Weekly reported on Sunday.

A stable and prosperous local market helped Shanghai's retail sector shine while other regions of the country suffered from poor sales and weak management, the newspaper said, quoting the Shanghai Commercial Commission.
Brisk growth of homegrown supermarket chains Hualian and Lianhua contributed to the impressive growth figures, it said, with each company having opened more than 100 outlets in the city.
